tasks.short: Make objects and characters appear lifelike through visual manipulation.

steps.what: Choose the lifelike lighting, colour and motion intent for objects or characters
Set up scene lights, material nodes and reusable animation controls
Manipulate light, colour, texture, shadow, transparency and static images to create lifelike motion
Review motion and appearance in context and approve the complete shot revision
Commit the approved lifelike shot revision to the production asset repository

tasks.design: Reuse native light rigs, material-node groups and controls in the animation-software category of {OTHER}. The animator still creates and judges the lifelike appearance; only repeated setup and the approved asset-repository commitment are simplified.
tasks.previous_blocker: Compatible shots repeat technical rig and node setup before creative adjustment.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked assets and parameter presets can reuse that setup.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle motion, lighting and material interactions can look artificial in context.
tasks.human_edge: Judge visual plausibility and deliberately break realism when the story requires it.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated scene setup; visual decisions remain with the animator.

reach.task: Judge shot continuity in a sequence

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: animation software supports reusable light rigs, node groups and linked assets; creative appearance and motion decisions remain human.

assumptions: Boundary covers a shot's appearance work and internal asset registration, not external release. Shares are provisional; rendering runtime is excluded from human labour.

Production supplies scene geometry, camera, frame range, colour-space settings and asset versions. s1 assesses the shot; s2 manually chooses and adapts compatible existing rigs. Missing or incompatible rigs require manual setup.
s3 retains all artistic manipulation time; s2 saves only repeated node and control construction. Test native presets and linking before scripts. This does not assume a reusable artistic answer.

{OTHER} also includes the production asset repository. s4 checks the exact scene revision and dependencies before s5 registers it; changed assets invalidate approval. Existing automatic registration earns no new saving.
research_questions: Which setup operations repeat without constraining the animator's visual choices?

already_counted.description: Review and approve final shot revision

incremental.description: Maintain compatible rigs and dependency checks

approvals.approved_version: Complete shot revision and linked-asset versions approved in s4; changes void registration approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes eight repeated-setup and five registration hours less two upkeep. Low assumes bespoke rigs and existing automatic registration, leaving upkeep only. All creative manipulation and appearance checking remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create storyboards mapping animation flow, key scenes and characters.

steps.what: Apply story development and directing to choose animation beats, scenes and characters
Draw storyboard panels showing key scenes, characters, staging and camera choices
Arrange storyboard panels and timing to show the animation's narrative flow
Review cinematography, continuity and editing rhythm and approve the complete storyboard
Register the approved storyboard revision in the production asset repository

tasks.design: Use native drawing libraries and panel-sequence controls in the storyboarding category of {OTHER}. Reuse repeated visual components and panel layout while preserving story, staging and rhythm choices; gate registration of the finished board.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated characters and panel formatting consume time alongside original drawing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native symbols, layers and panel templates can reuse existing material without generating story decisions.
tasks.still_hard: A sequence of attractive panels may fail to communicate the action or emotion.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a camera and edit rhythm that make the story readable.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated drawing and panel layout; narrative direction is unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: storyboarding tools support reusable drawings and native panel sequencing; narrative staging and pacing still require artistic judgement.

assumptions: Boundary ends at internal storyboard registration, not client approval or film publication. Shares are provisional; story-specific creative work remains fully counted.

The production supplies script, character sheets and existing rights-cleared drawings. s1 decides shot purpose and order; s2 manually picks reusable elements and redraws unique poses or staging in retained time.

s3 saves only recurring panel placement and layout; timing and narrative choices remain in retained time. No clean machine-readable shot list is assumed: s1 captures sequence decisions during its full work.
Test native libraries and templates first. {OTHER} includes the internal asset repository. The exact panel sequence and timing revision exists before s4 approval, and any change invalidates s5.
research_questions: Can existing drawings be reused without harming pose, staging or sequence clarity?

already_counted.description: Review complete board continuity and approve revision

incremental.description: Maintain reusable drawing libraries and layout presets

approvals.approved_version: Exact storyboard panels, order, timing and dependency revision approved in s4; edits void registration approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten repeated-drawing, six repeated-layout and five registration hours less two upkeep. Low assumes wholly original panels and existing layout/registration automation, leaving upkeep only. Narrative and continuity judgement retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Script, plan and create animated narrative sequences under deadlines.

steps.what: Script animated narrative sequences to meet the story brief and deadline
Plan sequence timing, drawing requirements and production effort
Draw key poses and original narrative artwork by hand
Create animated narrative sequences using drawing layers, keyframes and repeated motion
Check sequence performance and continuity and approve the complete animation revision
Commit the approved narrative animation revision to the internal production repository

tasks.design: Use native reusable motion cycles and layer templates in the animation-software category of {OTHER}. Retain scripting, planning, hand drawing and performance judgement, with a gate on the exact internal repository commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Simple repeated motion and layer setup are rebuilt alongside original performance work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native cycle reuse and scene templates can replace repeated manipulation where appropriate.
tasks.still_hard: Reused motion may feel mechanical or contradict the narrative beat.
tasks.human_edge: Create character performance and decide when repetition damages the story.
tasks.altitude: A modest reduction in repeated manipulation; narrative responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.task: Evaluate sequence pacing under a fixed duration

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: animation tools support reusable cycles and layer templates; original performance and story timing remain creative work.

assumptions: Boundary covers the animator's narrative sequence and internal commitment, not client delivery. Shares are provisional; no rendering runtime is counted.

s1 produces script and s2 records frame range, beat timing, intended poses and reusable asset choices during unchanged planning. s3 includes scanning or drawing-tablet capture when required; that physical capture is unchanged.

s4 manually imports drawings, establishes keys and adapts motion. Only repeated cycle manipulation and layer setup lose time; unique performance work remains. Test native tools before custom automation and give no saving to cycles already reused.

{OTHER} includes the internal production repository. s5 reviews the complete current sequence and dependencies before s6; edits invalidate approval. No other artist's work is transferred into this saving.
research_questions: Does cycle reuse reduce manipulation without increasing performance corrections?

incremental.description: Maintain reusable motion and dependency compatibility

approvals.approved_version: Exact sequence, timing and dependency revision approved in s5; any change requires new approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes six repeated-manipulation and five commitment hours less two upkeep. Low assumes unique movement and existing repository automation, leaving upkeep only. Script, plan, original drawing and sequence review retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop multimedia, promotional materials, illustrations and computer artwork.

steps.what: Clarify briefing, brochure, multimedia or technical illustration requirements and source accuracy
Choose the visual concept, hierarchy and appropriate illustration approach
Develop brochures, multimedia presentations, technical illustrations and computer artwork
Check accuracy, legibility and format behavior and approve the finished artwork package
Commit the approved artwork package to the internal production asset store

tasks.design: Configure native reusable layouts, symbols and format variants in the design-software category of {OTHER}. Keep visual concept and technical meaning human, then register only the reviewed final package in the asset-store category of {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Related formats repeat layout, approved graphics and resizing operations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked components and layout variants can reuse mechanical construction.
tasks.still_hard: A technically valid illustration may communicate the wrong procedure or fail at a small size.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what the audience must understand and verify that the artwork communicates it.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated format construction; visual and technical acceptance remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check technical illustration against product behavior

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: design software supports reusable symbols, linked layouts and format variants; technical meaning and audience suitability require human review.

assumptions: Boundary covers production of an internal artwork package, including relevant output files, not external web publication or printing. Shares are provisional and depend on recurring formats rather than wholly unique commissions.

Requesters supply purpose, audience, content, output size and technical source revision. s1 resolves missing requirements. s2 selects concept; s3 manually links source assets and adapts unique content while native layouts handle repeated construction and export settings.

No clean variant table is assumed or created for free: s3 includes selecting each required format and checking field placement. Test native linked components before custom generators. No model invents technical diagrams.
s4 checks the actual finished output files, not a pre-export design; s5 commits that exact package. Any correction returns to review. Existing format automation earns no additional saving.
research_questions: What proportion of construction repeats across formats after native templates already in use?

already_counted.description: Verify and approve finished multiformat package

incremental.description: Maintain templates and output-format regression examples

approvals.approved_version: Exact finished artwork-package files and source revision approved in s4; changed files require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 18 repeated-construction and five registration hours less two upkeep. Low assumes unique formats and existing asset registration, leaving upkeep only. Brief clarification, concept choices and finished-output checks stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reuse native production mechanics while retaining narrative, visual and technical choices.
role.ambitious_version: Produce consistent variants with less repetitive construction and unchanged creative accountability.
